summary.text: Captain from Cyphus who led two and twenty ships, with the Enienes and the Peraebi staunch in fight — men who dwelt about wintry Dodona and the ploughland by lovely Titaressus.

story.text: Nestor's muster-roll sets Gouneus beside the Lapith captains: from Cyphus he brought the Enienes and Peraebi, peoples of the far north-west who made their homes about Dodona and the fair-flowing Titaressus, which pours his streams into the Peneius yet is not mixed with the silver eddies of that river.
